req.title: Redirect-to rejects invalid status code
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 400 when /redirect-to receives a status_code outside the 300-399 range.

doc.reasoning: The redirect_to handler in httpbin/core.py only sets a custom status_code when `status_code >= 300 and status_code < 400`. Outside that range it silently falls back to 302. However, R-HTTPBIN-026 states the system SHALL respond with HTTP 400 for out-of-range status codes. Reading the actual source carefully: the code does NOT return 400 — it silently ignores invalid codes and returns 302. The requirement says it SHOULD return 400, but the implementation does not. Our tests must faithfully test the REQUIREMENT (expected 400 on invalid codes) so they will kill mutants that change the boundary comparisons (>= 300, < 400). We cover: (1) a valid in-range code (positive/EP), (2) an out-of-range code below 300 (negative/NEG), (3) boundary at exactly 300 (BVA lower bound), (4) boundary at exactly 399 (BVA upper bound), (5) boundary at 299 (BVA lower-1), (6) boundary at 400 (BVA upper+1). For the positive case we assert the redirect is honoured with the exact status code. For negative/boundary-out cases we assert 400 per the requirement — these will also catch operator-flip mutations on the >= and < comparisons.

tests.name: test_redirect_to_valid_status_code_302_is_accepted
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
status_code=302 is within the 300-399 range
expected: Location header is set to http://example.com
trace: R-HTTPBIN-026: valid status_code in range must be accepted and used
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_to_valid_status_code_302_is_accepted():
    r = client.get('/redirect-to?url=http://example.com&status_code=302')
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers.get('Location') == 'http://example.com'

test_redirect_to_valid_status_code_302_is_accepted()
